summary: Hawaii is legal-with-permit for domesticated rats — not the flat ban earlier research suggested. Hawaii runs four animal lists under HAR Chapter 4-71: Prohibited, Restricted (research/exhibition), Restricted (private/commercial), and Conditionally Approved. Domesticated rats sit on the CONDITIONALLY APPROVED list (HAR §4-71-6.5), which means they can be imported and kept WITH a prior HDOA Plant Quarantine import permit (Form PQ-7), entering only through Honolulu and inspected at the Airport Animal Quarantine Facility — a standard administrative permit available to private keepers, not a research-only carve-out. The one genuine open question is species precision: the list covers 'domesticated rats' (clearly the fancy rat, R. norvegicus), and whether it extends by name to a domesticated/fancy R. rattus needs written HDOA confirmation (if not, R. rattus would fall to the default-prohibited bucket and need a case-by-case permit). Wild/feral Rattus remains an invasive pest under separate public-health law — a different regime from the import-permit system.

kit.problem: Good news first: keeping a pet rat in Hawaii is NOT flatly banned. Hawaii regulates animal imports through lists under Hawaii Administrative Rules (HAR) Chapter 4-71, and "domesticated rats" sit on the Conditionally Approved Animals list (HAR §4-71-6.5) — meaning they can be lawfully imported and kept WITH a prior Hawaii Department of Agriculture & Biosecurity (HDOA) Plant Quarantine import permit (Form PQ-7). Animals enter only through Honolulu and are inspected at the Airport Animal Quarantine Facility. The catch is a species-precision gap. The Conditionally Approved entry is for "domesticated rats," and HDOA's own supporting materials describe that as the laboratory/fancy Norway rat (Rattus norvegicus) — bred for generations under controlled conditions and unlikely to establish in the wild. A domesticated, captive-bred fancy roof rat (Rattus rattus) shares that same tame, indoor-only, never-released profile, but it is not named on the list, and the wild roof rat is exactly the invasive pest Hawaii fights. So an applicant for a domesticated R. rattus risks falling through a gap: not clearly covered by the "domesticated rats" entry, and an unlisted animal is prohibited by default. This is a bureaucratic reading/coverage question, not a flat statutory ban — the permitting pathway already exists and HDOA controls the list.
kit.ask: Ask HDOA, in writing, to clarify and (if needed) close the gap: (1) Confirm whether the HAR §4-71-6.5 Conditionally Approved "domesticated rats" entry already covers a domesticated/fancy Rattus rattus lineage, or only Rattus norvegicus. (2) If it does not currently cover domesticated R. rattus, add the domesticated/captive-bred R. rattus lineage to the Conditionally Approved entry, OR confirm that a private keeper may obtain a case-by-case import permit for domesticated R. rattus under HRS §150A-6.2. The relevant question is domestication, not wild ancestry: the dog descends from the wolf and the house cat from a wild felid, yet both are recognized as domestic animals because of generations bred for tameness, and a multi-generation captive-bred roof rat is domesticated in that same sense as the fancy Norway rat the list already covers — we ask the Department to weigh that, not to reach any particular result. (3) State the standard permit conditions, fee, and processing time for a few pet rats. Request a written determination you can rely on before importing.
kit.branch_note: Branch = (a) AGENCY, with a narrow rulemaking fallback — NOT a fight with the legislature. Here is the concrete reasoning. The statute (HRS §150A-6.2) does NOT ban rats; it delegates to the Board of Agriculture the power to maintain the prohibited/restricted/conditionally-approved lists and to issue permits with conditions. The substantive species lists live in administrative rule (HAR Chapter 4-71) and in the published Conditionally Approved list (AR-71C) — instruments HDOA owns. "Domesticated rats" are ALREADY on the Conditionally Approved (keep-with-permit) list, so there is no statute correctly banning pet rats that the agency is merely enforcing. The only live problem is whether HDOA reads "domesticated rats" to include a domesticated/fancy Rattus rattus or only Rattus norvegicus. That is a classic agency interpretation/coverage gap — fixable by the agency without the legislature: a written determination (declaratory clarification) that the entry covers domesticated R. rattus, or a case-by-case HRS §150A-6.2 permit, or, if HDOA insists the entry is genus-specific, a routine update to the Conditionally Approved list to name the domesticated R. rattus lineage. Because the lever is the agency's own list and permit power, appealing to HDOA is exactly the right move — this is the opposite of trying to get an agency to ignore a statute it is correctly applying. The legislature is NOT the first stop. Escalation to a HAR Chapter 4-71 amendment (which has a public-comment/rulemaking window) only becomes relevant IF HDOA both refuses to read the existing entry to cover domesticated R. rattus and declines a case-by-case permit. Start with the written agency inquiry; keep the rulemaking-comment route in reserve.

template.en:
To: Hawaii Department of Agriculture & Biosecurity, Plant Quarantine Branch

Re: Coverage of the Conditionally Approved "domesticated rats" entry for a domesticated Rattus rattus

I am a Hawaii resident seeking to keep a domesticated, captive-bred pet rat as an indoor companion animal, fully in compliance with state import rules. I understand "domesticated rats" are on the Conditionally Approved Animals list (HAR §4-71-6.5) and may be imported with a Plant Quarantine permit (Form PQ-7).

My question concerns species precision. The animals I keep are domesticated, captive-bred, hand-tame Rattus rattus — multi-generation pet lineages kept strictly indoors in enclosures and never released, indistinguishable in behavior and risk from the fancy Norway rat already covered. They are not wild-caught and pose no establishment risk. Domestication is a matter of an animal's breeding history, not its wild ancestry: the dog descends from the wolf and the house cat from a wild felid, yet both are recognized as domestic animals because of generations bred for tameness — and a captive-bred roof rat is domesticated in that same sense as the fancy rat.

Please confirm in writing: (1) Does the Conditionally Approved "domesticated rats" entry include a domesticated/fancy Rattus rattus lineage, or only Rattus norvegicus? (2) If it does not, may a private keeper obtain a permit for domesticated R. rattus under the same Conditionally Approved pathway or a case-by-case permit under HRS §150A-6.2 — or could the domesticated R. rattus lineage be added to the Conditionally Approved entry? (3) What permit conditions, fee, and processing time apply?

Thank you for a written determination I can rely on before importing.

[Your name]
[Your city, Hawaii]
[Your email / phone]

kit.confidence_notes: Verified via official HDOA (dab.hawaii.gov) pages on 2026-06-09: (1) the Plant Quarantine import-program page links Form PQ-7 (https://dab.hawaii.gov/pi/files/2012/12/pq-7_fillable.pdf) and confirms conditionally-approved animals are imported by permit for individual possession; (2) the Plant Quarantine Office Contacts page lists the Oahu main office (1849 Auiki St, Honolulu; 808-832-0566) and airport line (808-837-8413); (3) HAR §4-71-6.5 (via Cornell LII) confirms the rule delegates to separately published lists and requires a board-approved permit even for conditionally-approved animals — supporting the agency-lever classification. Strongly corroborated species point: HDOA-hosted supporting material and multiple secondary sources describe the Conditionally Approved \"domesticated rats\" as Rattus norvegicus (lab/fancy Norway rat), which is the basis for the species-trap concern about R. rattus. NOT fully verified: the exact verbatim wording of the rats entry in the current Conditionally Approved list (AR-71C) — the official PDF is a scanned image (JBIG2) that could not be text-extracted, so whether the live list says \"Rattus species,\" \"domesticated rats,\" or \"Rattus norvegicus\" specifically should be confirmed directly with HDOA. Also NOT independently confirmed: a dedicated permit-inquiry email (the contacts page posts phones/offices, not a permit email), so I deliberately used the official application page and contacts page rather than an unverified inbox; and the Salesforce-style portal URL in prior internal notes was not re-confirmed and is omitted in favor of the verified import-program page. No live bill, pending list, or open public-comment window was found, so time_sensitive is empty. This is a research aid, not legal advice; the binding answer is HDOA's written determination.

keep.why: Domesticated rats are on Hawaii's Conditionally Approved list (HAR §4-71-6.5 / AR-71C), NOT the Prohibited list — so they may be kept under a valid HDOA Plant Quarantine import permit (HRS §150A-6.2). Possession without a permit for a listed animal is unlawful; an animal on no list is prohibited by default. Confidence is medium because whether the 'domesticated rats' entry covers R. rattus by name (vs only R. norvegicus) needs HDOA confirmation.
keep.governing_law: HAR §4-71-6.5 (Conditionally Approved list); HRS §150A-6.2 (Board maintains list + issues permits).

breed.why: No express breeding prohibition in the public HAR 4-71 text, but each imported animal must be permitted, and the Board may attach permit conditions on reproduction, facility type, and disposition of offspring (HRS §150A-6.2 allows time/place/use/special-precaution conditions). Establishing a breeding colony should be cleared with HDOA first.

sell_give.why: HAR 4-71 is import-focused (the permit controls the introduction event); no provision specifically regulates intra-state sale/transfer of conditionally-approved animals already lawfully held. Whether a Hawaii recipient needs their own permit/documentation isn't specified publicly and likely turns on permit conditions — confirm with HDOA before transferring.

transport.why: Importing requires an HDOA Plant Quarantine permit (Form PQ-7) obtained in advance; rats/mice/guinea pigs/chinchillas enter ONLY through Honolulu International Airport and are submitted by the carrier to the Airport Animal Quarantine Holding Facility for inspection. No state law regulates transport OUT of Hawaii (airlines set their own policies). The permit is the gatekeeping mechanism. Never release.
transport.governing_law: HAR §4-71-6.5; HRS §150A-6.2; HDOA import procedure (Form PQ-7; Honolulu entry).

restrictions.summary: To bring/keep a domesticated rat in Hawaii, get an HDOA Plant Quarantine import permit (Form PQ-7) BEFORE importing; the animal enters only via Honolulu and is inspected at the Airport Animal Quarantine Facility. ⚠️ Confirm in writing that the Conditionally Approved 'domesticated rats' entry covers R. rattus specifically before relying on it. Never release a roof rat (feral Rattus is an invasive pest).
steps: Apply for an HDOA Plant Quarantine import permit (Form PQ-7) via the online portal or by mail, in advance
Confirm with HDOA whether domesticated R. rattus is covered by the Conditionally Approved list or needs a case-by-case 150A-6.2 permit

If R. rattus isn't named, can a private keeper obtain a permit for domesticated R. rattus under the same Conditionally Approved pathway or a case-by-case HRS §150A-6.2 special permit?
